matching_criterion_description: Severe expressive language delay out of proportion to motor delay, seen in 95-100% of index cases (14/14 in Gregor et al. 2018; 20/21 in Goel et al. 2026), where children exhibit absent or severely limited speech.
Infantile/childhood axial hypotonia (~62% penetrance in Goel et al. 2026 and Jansen et al. 2019).
Externalizing behavioral dysregulation, comprising hyperactivity, ADHD, impulsivity, or aggressive outbursts (~62-85% in Western cohorts).
Completely absent across reported cohorts (0/21 in Goel et al.; 0/12 in Pan et al., 2024). Presence of phocomelia, oligodactyly, or terminal limb deficiencies effectively excludes FBXO11.
Severe cyanotic heart disease, outflow tract defects, or heterotaxy are near-zero in penetrance. Only minor septal or transient findings have been reported (2/20, 4/21, 0/12).
Persistent, profound primary microcephaly (head circumference < -3 to -4 SD at birth) is atypical; head circumferences typically fall within the normal range or show mild-to-moderate deviations.
Progressive motor loss, dementia, or active loss of milestones without epilepsy argues against IDDFBA, which characteristically presents as a static neurodevelopmental delay.
